    "question": "A first-order reaction reaches 75% completion in $40.0\\,\\mathrm{min}$ at temperature $T_1$. At temperature $T_2$, its rate constant is twice that at $T_1$. How long will a fresh sample take to reach 87.5% completion at $T_2$?",
    "options": [
      "$15.0\\,\\mathrm{min}$",
      "$20.0\\,\\mathrm{min}$",
      "$30.0\\,\\mathrm{min}$",
      "$60.0\\,\\mathrm{min}$"
    ],
    "correctIndex": 2,
    "answer": "Option C is correct. At $T_1$, 75% completion means that the fraction remaining is $0.25=(1/2)^2$, so two half-lives take $40.0\\,\\mathrm{min}$. Thus $t_{1/2,1}=20.0\\,\\mathrm{min}$. Since $t_{1/2}=\\ln 2/k$ and $k_2=2k_1$, the half-life at $T_2$ is $t_{1/2,2}=10.0\\,\\mathrm{min}$. For 87.5% completion, the fraction remaining is $0.125=(1/2)^3$, requiring three half-lives. Therefore, the required time is $3\\times10.0=30.0\\,\\mathrm{min}$. Award 1 mark for selecting option C.",
